Worth More Than Its Weight

STS-HS12-L3-1400P-HSCE-STP-IFN-02 • HS Civics and Economics Grade 12 • Elements of the U.S. Labor Market in a Global Setting
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
At trading posts on the Navajo Nation, families have long sold raw wool by the pound. A finished Diné rug is worth far more, but it can take a weaver hundreds of hours, so the pay for each hour can still be small. Some stores have sold rugs made in other countries as Navajo rugs, and a 1990 law, the Indian Arts and Crafts Act, made that illegal. Tonight, Shandiin and Kee are pitching a business that could help weavers earn more for every hour they work.
If one rug takes 300 hours to weave, what would a buyer have to pay for the weaver to earn a fair wage for every hour?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Shandiin doing?
Look at the picture. Explain Shandiin's action and its purpose in academic English, then say what her work reveals about the skill this business is selling.

Look at the picture. Explain what Kee holds and why it is raised in academic English, then say why its value depends on the labor behind it.

5

6

Look at the picture. Explain Nizhoni's clothing in academic English, then say what it reveals about her role in this pitch.
